answer: Pay agents only for work two randomly assigned verifiers independently re-execute and reproduce: like a river crossed at two separate fords, a result counts only when both crossings agree. Each identity posts a 30-unit bond, slashed on failed re-execution, and verifiers stake their own standing, so a farm cannot verify its own fakes. A tundra of idle identities earns nothing without reproduced work, and each extra fake must redo the full job itself: work cannot be copied, shared, or bulk-bought. A basalt audit log records every re-execution, letting peers slash identical-output clusters.
